name: OSS Document Scanner
why: Everyone has scanned a form with a phone and hit CamScanner's watermark/paywall; this does auto-crop, OCR and PDF export for free.
catch: Small team (≈7 recent authors); price taken from App Store in-app purchase list, not a vendor pricing page; overlaps a little with posted pdfcraft (PDF tools) but the job is scanning, not editing.

name: Seal
job: Saves any video to your phone
why: Saving videos from YouTube/Instagram/TikTok is a mass want, and Seal does it from the share sheet for free.
catch: Android only; downloading may break platform ToS; close-ish to posted Flow (YouTube client), avoid YouTube-only framing.

name: darktable
why: Lightroom is the default photo-editing subscription for every hobby photographer; darktable is the mature free raw editor.
catch: Steeper learning curve than Lightroom; we already posted Compositor as a Photoshop replacement, so frame this strictly as Lightroom/raw editing.

name: Shotcut
why: Premiere is the best-known paid video editor and Shotcut is a full free timeline editor with 4K, filters and keyframes.
catch: Concat vs CapCut (video editing) underperformed, so lean on the Adobe price, not 'video editor'; README has only one screenshot (shotcut.org has more).
close_to: 004 Concat vs CapCut flopped (3 views): needs a strong demo

name: Saber
why: Goodnotes is the student iPad app; Saber does handwriting notes on every platform for free.
catch: Fewer templates/AI features than Goodnotes; Goodnotes' cheapest tier is cheap ($11.99/yr) so the hook number is small.

name: PowerToys
why: 140k-star Microsoft toolkit (window zones, text grabber, colour picker, awake, bulk rename) every Windows user should have.
catch: FancyZones overlaps posted Loop (window snapping) so lead with the other tools; it's made by Microsoft, which some viewers may not see as 'indie open source'.
close_to: 056 Loop (window snapping): pitch it as the Windows all-in-one

name: LeechBlock NG
why: Doom-scrolling is a relatable pain and Freedom is the best-known paid site blocker; LeechBlock does schedules and lockdowns free.
catch: Browser extension only (no phone/app blocking); README has no screenshots, use the add-on store screenshots.

name: OBS Studio
why: Every Twitch/YouTube streamer knows OBS and Streamlabs Ultra is the subscription upsell built on the same core.
catch: Many viewers already know OBS is free; README has no screenshots (obsproject.com does); some overlap with posted openscreen (screen recording).

name: LMMS
why: FL Studio is the beat-making app every bedroom producer knows; LMMS has the same pattern/piano-roll workflow free.
catch: No README screenshots (lmms.io has them); FL price is from the official page title 'From $99', not a per-edition table; less polished than FL.

name: Blender
why: Blender is the 3D tool behind countless viral renders and replaces pricey Cinema 4D/Maya subscriptions.
catch: Very well known already as free; Cinema 4D price could not be read on maxon.net (JS), $94.99/mo is from a reseller; GitHub repo is a mirror of projects.blender.org; mild overlap with posted Solidcraft (3D parts).

name: Ultimate Vocal Remover
why: Karaoke, covers and remixes all need stems, and UVR splits vocals/instruments locally with AI for free.
catch: Moises' pricing table is behind login, $3.99/mo is from third-party reviews; mostly one maintainer (only 2 recent commit authors); heavy download and slow on old PCs.

name: AppFlowy
why: Notion is the aesthetic productivity app of Instagram/TikTok, and AppFlowy copies docs, databases and kanban boards offline.
catch: Notes category is close to posted Joplin; Notion's free plan already covers most individuals, so the hook is weaker for solo users.

name: ExplorerPatcher
why: Hating the Windows 11 taskbar/start menu is common and this restores the Windows 10 look for free.
catch: Windows updates sometimes break it and some antiviruses flag it; StartAllBack is cheap so the money hook is small.

name: HandBrake
why: 'Video too big to send' is a daily pain and HandBrake is the classic free converter/compressor.
catch: Wondershare's page shows both $39.99 and $45.99 for the yearly plan; README has no screenshots (handbrake.fr has them); slightly close to posted Filee (file converter).

name: AltTab
why: Every Windows-to-Mac switcher misses alt-tab window previews; AltTab adds them free, same Mac-utility lane as winners Loop and Maccy.
catch: README only has an SVG illustration (alt-tab.app has real screenshots); small core team.

name: Krokiet (Czkawka)
why: Running out of disk space is universal and this finds duplicate photos, big files and similar images for free.
catch: Old Czkawka GUI is superseded by the new Krokiet app; MacPaw only states 'starting at $1.95/month'; close to posted PureMac (CleanMyMac) cleanup lane.

name: Loop Habit Tracker
why: Habit tracking is a mainstream self-improvement trend and Loop is the classic free, ad-free tracker with charts and widgets.
catch: Android only while Streaks is iPhone only; Streaks is cheap, so the hook number is small.

name: OpenToonz
why: Based on the software Studio Ghibli used; replaces Toon Boom for 2D animation, a hook anime fans click.
catch: README has no screenshots (opentoonz.github.io has them); steep learning curve; only ≈5 recent commit authors.

name: Stellarium
job: Shows every star in your sky
why: Point-and-learn astronomy is broadly cool, and Stellarium is the realistic free planetarium.
catch: Desktop only (Stellarium Mobile is a separate paid app, not this repo); SkySafari is on sale ($49.99 regular); README has no screenshots.

name: Syncthing
job: Syncs your files with no cloud
why: Dropbox is a famous subscription and Syncthing syncs folders between your own devices for free with no storage cap.
catch: No cloud copy and no iOS app; the UI is a web page, README has no screenshots; close in spirit to posted LocalSend (file transfer).

name: LinearMouse
job: Fixes your mouse on a Mac
why: Mac + normal mouse = reversed scrolling and acceleration pain; LinearMouse fixes it per device, a Loop/Maccy-style Mac annoyance fix.
catch: README has no screenshots (linearmouse.app has them); niche to Mac users with external mice.

name: TuxGuitar
why: Guitar Pro is the standard tab editor every guitarist knows; TuxGuitar opens .gp files and plays them back free.
catch: Guitar Pro's live store page could not be read; €69.95 is from official blog/store snippets via search; old-looking UI; no README screenshots.

name: Surge XT
why: Serum is the most famous synth plugin among producers; Surge XT is a pro-grade free wavetable synth.
catch: Needs a DAW to host the plugin (pairs with LMMS); producer niche; no README screenshots.
